original_question: If U and V are real analytic domains in C^n, not assumed pseudoconvex, and f:U -> V is biholomorphic, does f extend continuously to the closure U-bar?
correct_elements: Your draft correctly targets the boundary-extension problem for biholomorphic maps between domains in complex Euclidean space. In particular, it captures the central theme of asking whether a biholomorphism extends from the interior to the boundary/closure.
missing_details: The paper's official question is quantified as 'Does every biholomorphic mapping ... ?' rather than asking about one fixed map in isolation.
The domains are assumed to be bounded.
The domains are assumed to be smoothly bounded, i.e. to have C^\infty boundaries.
Pseudoconvexity is an essential hypothesis in the paper's formulation; the paper does not remove it in Question 11.13.
The conclusion sought is not mere continuity to \overline{\Omega_1}; it is extension to a C^\infty diffeomorphism of the closures.
The extension is between both closures, namely \overline{\Omega_1} \to \overline{\Omega_2}.
The 'real analytic' hypothesis in your draft does not belong to Question 11.13; it comes from the immediately following real-analytic questions beginning with Question 11.14.
refined_question: Let \Omega_1, \Omega_2 \subset \mathbb{C}^n be bounded pseudoconvex domains with C^\infty boundaries, and let f:\Omega_1 \to \Omega_2 be biholomorphic. Must f extend to a C^\infty diffeomorphism \overline{\Omega_1} \to \overline{\Omega_2}?
justification: Within arXiv:math/9509202, the nearest official formulation is Section 11, Question 11.13 (p. 191). Your draft has the right general subject, but it broadens and shifts the problem in several paper-unfaithful ways: it drops boundedness and smooth boundary regularity, removes pseudoconvexity, inserts a real-analytic assumption, and weakens the conclusion from a C^\infty diffeomorphism of closures to mere continuity on one closure. The paragraph immediately before Question 11.13 (p. 190) explains the motivation via the Bell-Ligocka theorem and shows why the official formulation asks for diffeomorphic extension of closures. The sentence immediately after Question 11.13 starts a separate 'real analytic theory' with Question 11.14, so the real-analytic language in the draft appears to have been imported from the next question rather than from the mapping problem itself.
